<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Seaweed FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-seaweed" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-seaweed" data-question="What heavy metals are found in seaweed?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in seaweed?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Arsenic, cadmium, lead and mercury are measured in most seaweed surveys, and arsenic is present at the highest concentrations.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Most of that arsenic is organic; inorganic arsenic is high mainly in hijiki and a few kelps, while cadmium is highest in laver and wakame.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rose M, Lewis J, Langford N, Baxter M, Origgi S, Barber M, MacBain H, Thomas K · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Arsenic in seaweed—Forms, concentration and dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Chemical Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Duinker A, Kleppe M, Fjare E, Biancarosa I, Heldal HE, Dahl L, Lunestad BT · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Knowledge update on macroalgae food and feed safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Rapport fra Havforskningen</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-seaweed" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-seaweed" data-question="How do heavy metals get into seaweed?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into seaweed?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Seaweed absorbs metals from the surrounding seawater through its whole surface.<sup class="cite">[[sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Duinker A, Kleppe M, Fjare E, Biancarosa I, Heldal HE, Dahl L, Lunestad BT · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Knowledge update on macroalgae food and feed safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Rapport fra Havforskningen</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cherry2019-edible-seaweeds-risks-benefits|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cherry P, O&#39;Hara C, Magee PJ, McSorley EM, Allsopp PJ · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cherry2019-edible-seaweeds-risks-benefits">Risks and benefits of consuming edible seaweeds</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nutrition Reviews</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cherry2019-edible-seaweeds-risks-benefits">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Brown seaweeds take up arsenate like phosphate and turn most of it into arsenosugars, while hijiki keeps much of it as inorganic arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/huang2020-hijiki-arsenic-growth-stages|22]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Huang SX, Jiang Q, Ding YF, Wang FJ, Zhu C · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/huang2020-hijiki-arsenic-growth-stages">Arsenic contents and speciation at different growth stages of Sargassum fusiforme [Harv.] Setchell (Hijiki), an edible seaweed</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Ecology and Environmental Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/huang2020-hijiki-arsenic-growth-stages">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/garcia-salgado2012-edible-algae-arsenic-speciation|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">García-Salgado S, Quijano MA, Bonilla MM · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/garcia-salgado2012-edible-algae-arsenic-speciation">Arsenic speciation in edible alga samples by microwave-assisted extraction and high performance liquid chromatography coupled to atomic fluorescence spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Analytica Chimica Acta</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/garcia-salgado2012-edible-algae-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-organic-seaweed-free-from-heavy-metals" data-anchor="is-organic-seaweed-free-from-heavy-metals" data-question="Is organic seaweed free from heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is organic seaweed free from heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No source in the library compares organic-certified and conventional seaweed, so there is no evidence that an organic label lowers metals. Metal levels follow the seaweed type and the water it grew in, which certification does not control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Duinker A, Kleppe M, Fjare E, Biancarosa I, Heldal HE, Dahl L, Lunestad BT · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Knowledge update on macroalgae food and feed safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Rapport fra Havforskningen</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/hahn2022-salish-seaweed-contaminants|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Hahn ME, Schultz IR, Ylitalo GM, Boyd D, Sloan CA, Niewolny LA, Bolton JL, Haigh T, Incardona JP · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hahn2022-salish-seaweed-contaminants">Chemical contaminant levels in edible seaweeds of the Salish Sea and implications for their consumption</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLOS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/hahn2022-salish-seaweed-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-seaweed-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-seaweed-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of seaweed have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of seaweed have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For inorganic arsenic, nori, wakame, dulse and Saccharina kombu were lowest, and hijiki highest.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au">Survey of Inorganic Arsenic in Seaweed and Seaweed-Containing Products Available in Australia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Australia New Zealand (FSANZ), Survey report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Duinker A, Kleppe M, Fjare E, Biancarosa I, Heldal HE, Dahl L, Lunestad BT · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Knowledge update on macroalgae food and feed safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Rapport fra Havforskningen</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, kombu and dulse were lower than laver and wakame, so no type is lowest for every metal.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-produce-seaweed-with-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-regions-produce-seaweed-with-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which regions produce seaweed with the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions produce seaweed with the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Origin comparisons are few. One Canary Islands survey found Galician kombu and wakame lower in cadmium than Asian products, and Korean west-coast laver higher than south-coast laver, but species differences are far larger than these origin differences.<sup class="cite">[[sources/martinleon2021-edible-seaweeds-canary-metals-nitrates|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Martín-León V, Paz S, D&#39;Eufemia PA, Plasencia JJ, Sagratini G, Marcantoni G, Navarro-Romero M, Gutiérrez ÁJ, Hardisson A, Rubio-Armendáriz C · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/martinleon2021-edible-seaweeds-canary-metals-nitrates">Human Exposure to Toxic Metals (Cd, Pb, Hg) and Nitrates (NO3−) from Seaweed Consumption</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Sciences</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/martinleon2021-edible-seaweeds-canary-metals-nitrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/hwang2010-dried-seaweed-korea-metals|26]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Hwang YO, Park SG, Park GY, Choi SM, Kim MY · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hwang2010-dried-seaweed-korea-metals">Total arsenic, mercury, lead, and cadmium contents in edible dried seaweed in Korea</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B: Surveillance</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/hwang2010-dried-seaweed-korea-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-products-made-from-seaweed-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-anchor="do-products-made-from-seaweed-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-question="Do products made from seaweed also contain heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do products made from seaweed also contain heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Seaweed supplements can, because they are concentrated dried seaweed: one Belgian kelp supplement carried 4.7 mg/kg inorganic arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cheyns2021-algae-cyanobacteria-supplements-arsenic|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cheyns K, Demaegdt H, Waegeneers N, Ruttens A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cheyns2021-algae-cyanobacteria-supplements-arsenic">Intake of food supplements based on algae or cyanobacteria may pose a health risk due to elevated concentrations of arsenic species</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cheyns2021-algae-cyanobacteria-supplements-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Foods that contain seaweed, such as snacks or sushi, were not measured together with their seaweed, so their results cannot be attributed to it.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fechner2022-bfr-meal-hg-cd-pb-ni-germany|38]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Fechner C, Hackethal C, Höpfner T, Dietrich J, Bloch D, Lindtner O, Sarvan I · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fechner2022-bfr-meal-hg-cd-pb-ni-germany">Results of the BfR MEAL Study: In Germany, mercury is mostly contained in fish and seafood while cadmium, lead, and nickel are present in a broad spectrum of foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Chemistry: X</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fechner2022-bfr-meal-hg-cd-pb-ni-germany">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-do-the-levels-in-seaweed-mean-for-health" data-anchor="what-do-the-levels-in-seaweed-mean-for-health" data-question="What do the levels in seaweed mean for health?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What do the levels in seaweed mean for health?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For most people seaweed adds little to metal intake because portions are small.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/song2017-china-dietary-cadmium-exposure|35]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Song Y, Wang Y, Mao W, Sui H, Yong L, Yang D, Jiang D, Zhang L, Gong Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/song2017-china-dietary-cadmium-exposure">Dietary cadmium exposure assessment among the Chinese population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE 12(5): e0177978</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/song2017-china-dietary-cadmium-exposure">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Regular hijiki eaters are the exception: EFSA estimated about 1.6 µg/kg body weight per day of inorganic arsenic for high consumers, and several food agencies advise against eating hijiki.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rose M, Lewis J, Langford N, Baxter M, Origgi S, Barber M, MacBain H, Thomas K · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Arsenic in seaweed—Forms, concentration and dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Chemical Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|36]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs">Chronic dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-seaweed" data-anchor="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-seaweed" data-question="Are there legal limits for heavy metals in seaweed?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are there legal limits for heavy metals in seaweed?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, in some markets: Australia and New Zealand set 1 mg/kg inorganic arsenic at 85% hydration, Singapore 2 ppm inorganic arsenic and cadmium, Thailand 2 mg/kg cadmium for dried seaweed, and China 0.5–1.0 mg/kg lead for algae.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2024-schedule-19-contaminants|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2024-schedule-19-contaminants">Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code - Schedule 19 - Maximum levels of contaminants and natural toxicants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Federal Register of Legislation, Authorised Version F2024C00908</span><a <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="can-soaking-or-cooking-remove-heavy-metals-from-seaweed" data-anchor="can-soaking-or-cooking-remove-heavy-metals-from-seaweed" data-question="Can soaking or cooking remove heavy metals from seaweed?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Can soaking or cooking remove heavy metals from seaweed?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Soaking and boiling remove much of the arsenic, especially from hijiki, as long as the water is thrown away.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ichikawa2006-hijiki-cooking-arsenic|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ichikawa S, Kamoshida M, Hanaoka K, Hamano M, Maitani T, Kaise T · 2006</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ichikawa2006-hijiki-cooking-arsenic">Decrease of arsenic in edible brown algae Hijikia fusiforme by the cooking process</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ichikawa2006-hijiki-cooking-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/laparra2003-seaweed-arsenic-bioaccessibility|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Laparra JM, Velez D, Montoro R, Barbera R, Farre R · 2003</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/laparra2003-seaweed-arsenic-bioaccessibility">Estimation of Arsenic Bioaccessibility in Edible Seaweed by an in Vitro Digestion Method</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/laparra2003-seaweed-arsenic-bioaccessibility">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ownsworth2019-estuarine-macroalgae-elements|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ownsworth E, Selby D, Ottley CJ, Unsworth E, Raab A, Feldmann J, Sproson AD, Kuroda J, Faidutti C, Bucker P · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ownsworth2019-estuarine-macroalgae-elements">Tracing the natural and anthropogenic influence on the trace elemental chemistry of estuarine macroalgae and the implications for human consumption</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Science of the Total Environment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ownsworth2019-estuarine-macroalgae-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> They do little for cadmium and lead, which stayed the same or rose on a dry-weight basis after processing sugar kelp.<sup class="cite">[[sources/sund2026-saccharina-pte-processing|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Sund R, Holdt S L, Bang-Berthelsen C H, Stevant P, Sloth J J, Skipnes D · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sund2026-saccharina-pte-processing">Pulsed electric field processing as an alternative to warm water treatment for the reduction of potentially toxic elements in Saccharina latissima</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Applied Phycology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sund2026-saccharina-pte-processing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/groleau2025-inuit-fish-broth-metals-pregnancy|27]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Groleau T, Lemire M, Ponton DE, Amyot M · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/groleau2025-inuit-fish-broth-metals-pregnancy">Improving nutritional intakes and reducing metal(loid) exposures from wild fish broth among Inuit pregnant women</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Science of the Total Environment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/groleau2025-inuit-fish-broth-metals-pregnancy">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-is-the-difference-between-total-and-inorganic-arsenic-in-seaweed" data-anchor="what-is-the-difference-between-total-and-inorganic-arsenic-in-seaweed" data-question="What is the difference between total and inorganic arsenic in seaweed?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What is the difference between total and inorganic arsenic in seaweed?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Total arsenic counts every form, and in seaweed most of it is organic arsenosugars, which are much less toxic than inorganic arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/garcia-salgado2012-edible-algae-arsenic-speciation|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">García-Salgado S, Quijano MA, Bonilla MM · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/garcia-salgado2012-edible-algae-arsenic-speciation">Arsenic speciation in edible alga samples by microwave-assisted extraction and high performance liquid chromatography coupled to atomic fluorescence spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Analytica Chimica Acta</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/garcia-salgado2012-edible-algae-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Limits and health assessments for seaweed are written for inorganic arsenic, so a total arsenic result alone cannot show compliance.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2024-schedule-19-contaminants|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2024-schedule-19-contaminants">Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code - Schedule 19 - Maximum levels of contaminants and natural toxicants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Federal Register of Legislation, Authorised Version F2024C00908</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2024-schedule-19-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/sfa2026-food-regulations-heavy-metals|29]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Singapore Food Agency · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sfa2026-food-regulations-heavy-metals">Food Regulations: regulation 31 heavy metals, arsenic and lead</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Singapore Statutes Online</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sfa2026-food-regulations-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="should-pregnant-women-or-children-avoid-any-seaweed" data-anchor="should-pregnant-women-or-children-avoid-any-seaweed" data-question="Should pregnant women or children avoid any seaweed?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Should pregnant women or children avoid any seaweed?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The supported advice concerns hijiki: food agencies in the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand advised against eating it because of its inorganic arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rose M, Lewis J, Langford N, Baxter M, Origgi S, Barber M, MacBain H, Thomas K · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Arsenic in seaweed—Forms, concentration and dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Chemical Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs|42]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA, Arcella D, Cascio C, Gómez Ruiz JA · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs">Chronic dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A review also cites Australian and New Zealand advice for pregnant women to limit brown seaweed to one portion a week.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cherry2019-edible-seaweeds-risks-benefits|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cherry P, O&#39;Hara C, Magee PJ, McSorley EM, Allsopp PJ · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cherry2019-edible-seaweeds-risks-benefits">Risks and benefits of consuming edible seaweeds</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nutrition Reviews</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cherry2019-edible-seaweeds-risks-benefits">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="should-i-stop-eating-seaweed" data-anchor="should-i-stop-eating-seaweed" data-question="Should I stop eating seaweed?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Should I stop eating seaweed?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The evidence supports avoiding hijiki, not seaweed in general.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rose M, Lewis J, Langford N, Baxter M, Origgi S, Barber M, MacBain H, Thomas K · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Arsenic in seaweed—Forms, concentration and dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Chemical Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Nori, wakame and kombu measured far lower in inorganic arsenic, though nori and wakame carry more cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au">Survey of Inorganic Arsenic in Seaweed and Seaweed-Containing Products Available in Australia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Australia New Zealand (FSANZ), Survey report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="why-is-hijiki-so-much-higher-in-arsenic-than-other-seaweeds" data-anchor="why-is-hijiki-so-much-higher-in-arsenic-than-other-seaweeds" data-question="Why is hijiki so much higher in arsenic than other seaweeds?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Why is hijiki so much higher in arsenic than other seaweeds?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Hijiki keeps much of the arsenic it absorbs as inorganic arsenate instead of converting it to arsenosugars.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rose M, Lewis J, Langford N, Baxter M, Origgi S, Barber M, MacBain H, Thomas K · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Arsenic in seaweed—Forms, concentration and dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Chemical Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/garcia-salgado2012-edible-algae-arsenic-speciation|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">García-Salgado S, Quijano MA, Bonilla MM · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/garcia-salgado2012-edible-algae-arsenic-speciation">Arsenic speciation in edible alga samples by microwave-assisted extraction and high performance liquid chromatography coupled to atomic fluorescence spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Analytica Chimica Acta</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/garcia-salgado2012-edible-algae-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> About 60–70% of its total arsenic is inorganic, against under 1% in most kelp and nori.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rose M, Lewis J, Langford N, Baxter M, Origgi S, Barber M, MacBain H, Thomas K · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Arsenic in seaweed—Forms, concentration and dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Chemical Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rose2007-seaweed-arsenic-forms-uk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/taylor2016-new-england-seaweed-arsenic|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Taylor VF, Jackson BP · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/taylor2016-new-england-seaweed-arsenic">Concentrations and speciation of arsenic in New England seaweed species harvested for food and agriculture</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemosphere</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/taylor2016-new-england-seaweed-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-kelp-or-kombu-high-in-arsenic" data-anchor="is-kelp-or-kombu-high-in-arsenic" data-question="Is kelp or kombu high in arsenic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is kelp or kombu high in arsenic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Kombu is high in total arsenic but usually low in inorganic arsenic, around 0.2 mg/kg as sold.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au">Survey of Inorganic Arsenic in Seaweed and Seaweed-Containing Products Available in Australia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Australia New Zealand (FSANZ), Survey report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Oarweed (Laminaria digitata) is the exception, with 8–62 mg/kg inorganic arsenic dry weight in studies from Norway, Ireland and Maine.<sup class="cite">[[sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Duinker A, Kleppe M, Fjare E, Biancarosa I, Heldal HE, Dahl L, Lunestad BT · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Knowledge update on macroalgae food and feed safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Rapport fra Havforskningen</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/taylor2016-new-england-seaweed-arsenic|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Taylor VF, Jackson BP · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/taylor2016-new-england-seaweed-arsenic">Concentrations and speciation of arsenic in New England seaweed species harvested for food and agriculture</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemosphere</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/taylor2016-new-england-seaweed-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ronan2017-laminaria-ascophyllum-ias-ireland|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ronan JM, Stengel DB, Raab A, Feldmann J, O&#39;Hea L, Bralatei E, McGovern E · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ronan2017-laminaria-ascophyllum-ias-ireland">High proportions of inorganic arsenic in Laminaria digitata but not in Ascophyllum nodosum samples from Ireland</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemosphere</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ronan2017-laminaria-ascophyllum-ias-ireland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-nori-high-in-cadmium" data-anchor="is-nori-high-in-cadmium" data-question="Is nori high in cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is nori high in cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Nori is among the higher cadmium seaweeds.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/hwang2010-dried-seaweed-korea-metals|26]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Hwang YO, Park SG, Park GY, Choi SM, Kim MY · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hwang2010-dried-seaweed-korea-metals">Total arsenic, mercury, lead, and cadmium contents in edible dried seaweed in Korea</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B: Surveillance</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/hwang2010-dried-seaweed-korea-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Dried laver averaged 1.68 mg/kg in European monitoring and Korean laver 0.61 mg/kg dry weight, near or above the 0.5–2 mg/kg limits used in some markets.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/hwang2010-dried-seaweed-korea-metals|26]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Hwang YO, Park SG, Park GY, Choi SM, Kim MY · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hwang2010-dried-seaweed-korea-metals">Total arsenic, mercury, lead, and cadmium contents in edible dried seaweed in Korea</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B: Surveillance</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/hwang2010-dried-seaweed-korea-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/sfa2026-food-regulations-heavy-metals|29]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Singapore Food Agency · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sfa2026-food-regulations-heavy-metals">Food Regulations: regulation 31 heavy metals, arsenic and lead</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Singapore Statutes Online</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sfa2026-food-regulations-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-fresh-seaweed-lower-in-metals-than-dried" data-anchor="is-fresh-seaweed-lower-in-metals-than-dried" data-question="Is fresh seaweed lower in metals than dried?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is fresh seaweed lower in metals than dried?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Fresh seaweed has lower concentrations per kilogram only because it is mostly water.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au">Survey of Inorganic Arsenic in Seaweed and Seaweed-Containing Products Available in Australia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Australia New Zealand (FSANZ), Survey report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2012-seaweed-inorganic-arsenic-au">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European fresh kombu averaged 0.20 mg/kg cadmium against 0.46 mg/kg for dried kombu, which reflects water content rather than a cleaner product.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Dujardin B, Ferreira de Sousa R, Gomez Ruiz JA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Dietary exposure to heavy metals and iodine intake via consumption of seaweeds and halophytes in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-farmed-seaweed-lower-in-metals-than-wild" data-anchor="is-farmed-seaweed-lower-in-metals-than-wild" data-question="Is farmed seaweed lower in metals than wild?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is farmed seaweed lower in metals than wild?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Not consistently. Farmed and wild sugar kelp in New England had similar cadmium and total arsenic, and farmed sugar kelp in northern Norway carried more cadmium than southern farms.<sup class="cite">[[sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Duinker A, Kleppe M, Fjare E, Biancarosa I, Heldal HE, Dahl L, Lunestad BT · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Knowledge update on macroalgae food and feed safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Rapport fra Havforskningen</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shaughnessy2023-sugar-kelp-new-england-metals|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shaughnessy B K, Jackson B P, Byrnes J E K · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shaughnessy2023-sugar-kelp-new-england-metals">Evidence of elevated heavy metals concentrations in wild and farmed sugar kelp (Saccharina latissima) in New England</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shaughnessy2023-sugar-kelp-new-england-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-seaweed-contain-mercury" data-anchor="does-seaweed-contain-mercury" data-question="Does seaweed contain mercury?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does seaweed contain mercury?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Usually very little.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Duinker A, Kleppe M, Fjare E, Biancarosa I, Heldal HE, Dahl L, Lunestad BT · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Knowledge update on macroalgae food and feed safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Rapport fra Havforskningen</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/duinker2020-macroalgae-food-feed-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Most dried-seaweed mercury results in GEMS/Food were below a 50 µg/kg detection limit, and Norwegian medians were 0.005–0.024 mg/kg dry weight.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-kelp-supplements-a-concern" data-anchor="are-kelp-supplements-a-concern" data-question="Are kelp supplements a concern?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are kelp supplements a concern?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

They can be, because supplements are dried seaweed taken daily.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cheyns2021-algae-cyanobacteria-supplements-arsenic|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cheyns K, Demaegdt H, Waegeneers N, Ruttens A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cheyns2021-algae-cyanobacteria-supplements-arsenic">Intake of food supplements based on algae or cyanobacteria may pose a health risk due to elevated concentrations of arsenic species</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cheyns2021-algae-cyanobacteria-supplements-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/nischwitz2006-commercial-kelp-arsenic-speciation|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nischwitz V, Pergantis SA · 2006</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nischwitz2006-commercial-kelp-arsenic-speciation">Improved Arsenic Speciation Analysis for Extracts of Commercially Available Edible Marine Algae Using HPLC-ES-MS/MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry 54(18):6507-6519</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nischwitz2006-commercial-kelp-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Belgian kelp supplements ranged from 0.07 to 4.7 mg/kg inorganic arsenic, and the EU caps cadmium at 3.0 mg/kg in supplements made mainly from seaweed.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cheyns2021-algae-cyanobacteria-supplements-arsenic|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cheyns K, Demaegdt H, Waegeneers N, Ruttens A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cheyns2021-algae-cyanobacteria-supplements-arsenic">Intake of food supplements based on algae or cyanobacteria may pose a health risk due to elevated concentrations of arsenic species</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cheyns2021-algae-cyanobacteria-supplements-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|33]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
